country: # Catalunya: kiting is banned on all Catalan beaches 1 Jun–30 Sep except in authorised kite zones.

name: Sant Pere Pescador
notes: Kite areas of about 200 m each: Cortal de la Vila (schools and free riding) and Cortal de la Devesa (run by the La Ballena Alegre campsite); authorised summer kite zone, stay in the marked channels. Tramuntana and summer thermal. Also: Empuriabrava – La Rubina (5 km north, easterlies).

name: Castelldefels
notes: Town kite zone 1 Jun–mid Sep at Platja de la Pineda, between Carrer 9 and Carrer 11: weekdays 15–19 h only (2026), closed weekends and holidays, free licence and vest from the office at Passeig Marítim 159. Outside those hours kiting is banned in summer. Free the rest of the year.

name: Riumar (Ebro delta)
notes: Mainly an autumn–spring spot: best in mestral (NW, cross-shore); summer southerlies are offshore. Schools ride a signposted zone; one guide says the beach is closed to kites in summer. Check the signs on site.

name: Platja dels Eucaliptus (Ebro delta)
notes: Shallow water at the root of the Trabucador, where the schools teach; beginner-friendly. In summer ride only the signposted kite zone.

name: El Trabucador (Ebro delta)
notes: Summer thermal (S) spot; flat, shallow water on the Badia dels Alfacs (west) side, about 1 m deep in places. Schools report signposted kite zones in summer.

country: # Comunitat Valenciana: summer kiting only in the few buoyed channels / zones.

name: Valencia – El Perellonet
notes: Municipal buoyed kite zone south of the Perellonet river mouth, open year-round; Kitezone club. Also: Sueca – Mareny de Barraquetes (summer channel for club members, free off-season).

name: Oliva
notes: Oliva Nova; in summer kiting only in the authorised zone (club rescue boat). Also: Dénia – Les Deveses (marked kite zone just south).

name: Santa Pola – La Gola
locate: q:Playa de La Gola Santa Pola
notes: La Gola open to kites year-round; neighbouring Playa Lisa is closed to kites in summer. Also: Elche – Arenales del Sol (north), Guardamar – Els Tossals (south).

name: Mar Menor – Los Narejos
notes: Flat-water lagoon, kite zone and school; E and SW (lebeche) most common. Also: Los Nietos (south shore, onshore in NE/E), La Manga – Isla del Ciervo.

name: Almerimar
notes: Poniente (W) spot by the marina: flat between the breakwaters, waves further out. Also: Roquetas de Mar – Las Salinas (levante).

name: Málaga – Los Álamos
notes: Official kite zone (Los Álamos / Guadalmar), moved during the bathing season; SW thermal Apr–Oct.

country: # Andalucía — Strait and Cádiz Atlantic coast

name: Tarifa – Los Lances
notes: Los Lances Norte (Río Jara–Waves). Summer: school and free-rider zones only, no kiting from Río Jara to town 15 Jun–15 Sep. Also: Tarifa – Balneario (experts only, rocks and currents; no kiting 15 Jun–15 Sep).

name: Tarifa – Valdevaqueros
notes: Includes Punta Paloma; summer kite zone is crowded; rocks at low tide. Also: Bolonia (no kiting in summer).

name: Los Caños de Meca
locate: q:Playa de Los Caños de Meca
notes: Levante spot; rocks towards the lighthouse at low tide; officially no kiting in summer.

name: El Palmar (Vejer)
locate: q:Playa de El Palmar Vejer de la Frontera
notes: Westerlies; ride the south end, watch surfers and bathers; rocks at low tide.

name: Chiclana – Sancti Petri
notes: Winter: free; summer only inside the water-sports channels. Also: San Fernando – Camposoto (westerlies), Cádiz – Cortadura (rocky, high tide).

name: El Portil
notes: Flat water behind the El Rompido sandspit (cross the Río Piedras); strong currents. Also: Punta Umbría (open beach, waves).

name: Doniños (Ferrol)
notes: Exposed Atlantic beach with waves; kite area is the left side of the bay (Punta Penencia). Best in N–NE cross-shore wind, S–SW gets rough fast; experienced riders. Local crowd is protective: ride respectfully. Alternative: San Xurxo.

name: Razo (Carballo)
notes: Open Atlantic beach with waves and strong currents, best in NE wind; winter SW is hard to control. Experienced riders. Inside the Razo–Baldaio nature reserve: the lagoon behind is flat at high tide but stay out of it as the tide drops (bird sanctuary, kite ban feared).

name: A Lanzada
notes: Huge exposed beach with clean waves; best in SW–W wind from autumn to spring. Intermediate and up; rocks in the water and to the south. A spot guide says kiting is not allowed here in summer (no official text found): check with the schools. Also: O Grove – A Mexilloeira (sheltered ría, flat in N–NE).

name: Redondela – Cesantes
notes: Flat shallow water at the head of the Vigo ría (San Simón inlet); SW summer thermal in the afternoon, gusty NE off the land in high pressure. Home of the TMKiteClub and the Kitefest. Boats on the south side, sharp mussels in the sand. Also: Vigo – O Vao (flat behind Toralla island in W–NW).

name: Salinas – San Juan de Nieva
notes: Strong wind and waves; advanced riders. Also: Gijón – El Arbeyal (sheltered, N–NE) and San Lorenzo (NE–E).

name: Somo
notes: Waves on the open beach; flat water in La Poza (Miera estuary) at low–mid tide, schools there.

name: Embalse de La Loteta
notes: Reservoir ridden in the cierzo (NW), which blows along its length; south launch area with Club Kitesurf La Loteta. Shallow and rocky in places: check the water level.

name: Mallorca – Pollença (Sa Marina)
notes: Authorised kite zone and schools in the Bay of Pollença.

name: Mallorca – Son Serra de Marina
locate: q:Platja de Son Serra de Marina
notes: Island's main kite beach Oct–May; summer restrictions. Also: Platja de Muro (small authorised channel).

name: Menorca – Cala Tirant
notes: Waves with the tramuntana (N); summer: designated launch area only.

name: Fuerteventura – Sotavento
notes: Lagoon at low tide (flat, knee-deep); open sea at high tide. World Cup venue. Also: Costa Calma (flatter water, fewer riders).

name: Lanzarote – Famara
notes: Waves, trade wind; currents.

name: Lanzarote – Costa Teguise
notes: Las Cucharas; waves, schools; gusty close to shore.

name: Gran Canaria – Pozo Izquierdo
notes: Very strong wind, waves, rocky: experts. Also: Vargas (trade wind, waves), Bahía Feliz (smaller waves, school).

name: Tenerife – El Médano
notes: Trade wind May–Oct; shallow water at the north end.
